Stellantis Is Pulling Out Of Every Racing Series It Competes In Except NASCAR

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (429 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stellantis is about to throw in the towel on just about every single one of its motorsports endeavors other than NASCAR...
  • Recent findings suggest that the moves come as the automaker cuts costs across the board at the behest of CEO Antonio Filosa, according to Reuters.
  • This isn't the first time something like this has happened for Peugeot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stellantis is about to throw in the towel on just about every single one of its motorsports endeavors other than NASCAR... which it just re-entered after a 14-year hiatus. On November 23, it's expected that the automaker will convene two extraordinary works council meetings with the ultimate outcome being a withdrawal. That means Peugeot would leave endurance racing (which admittedly hasn't been going too well), Citroën and Opel would drop out of Formula E, and Lancia's reborn rally team would bite the dust.

Recent findings suggest that the moves come as the automaker cuts costs across the board at the behest of CEO Antonio Filosa, according to Reuters. He's doing what he can to turn the organization around after years of falling sales and weakening profitability. Earlier this year, Filosa debuted a broad efficiency drive, known as the "Value Creation Program," and it targets about $6.6 billion in cost savings by 2028. Autocar reports that Stellantis Motorsport costs about $330 million a year to run, and cutting it could help with Stellantis' finances in Europe, where it just lost $341 million in the third quarter alone.

This isn't the first time something like this has happened for Peugeot. Its former owners, PSA, quit the 24 Hours of Le Mans back in 2012 in an effort to save cash, and it didn't rejoin until 2022.

It is, nevertheless, still strange timing. As I mentioned, Dodge just re-entered NASCAR. On top of that, French outlet L'Automobile reports that Peugeot has a redesigned 9x8 for its 2027 WEC endurance program and Citroën and Opel have been working on their upcoming Gen4 car for Formula E with new technical partners. It's likely that the team that runs Citroën, MSG Racing, will continue with a new sponsor.

Hell, Open is technically making its debut in FE this upcoming season. It was just declared in March of this year when the brand signed a four-year contract to compete with the latest Gen4 cars.

Recent findings suggest that lancia's WRC re-entry is another sacrificial lamb at the altar of financial prudence. The Lancia Corse HF team started in the WRC2 category this year, Autocar reports. It entered its gas-powered Ypsilon Rally2 HF Integrale, and it has even racked up a few wins. More likely than not, customer teams will continue to be supported, though.

In a recent development, motorsports are usually what's first to get cut when an automaker is struggling. Earlier this year, Alpine dropped out of WEC, citing a tough market, and Porsche did the same thing back in 2025.

#65111. The Ultimate Playbook To Buying a Home Without 20% Down Using Grants and Assistance Programs

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1926 w)

The Ultimate Playbook To Buying a Home Without 20% Down Using Grants and Assistance Programs

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1926 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Buying a home can be an intimidating process, with the biggest hurdle for many being coming up with enough funds for a down payment.
  • In a recent development, many people believe they need to put down at least 20% if they want a home.
  • Most buyers have down payments ranging from 3.5% to 20% of the sale price of the home they're buying, and there are many down payment assistance programs that can help aspiring homeowners pivot from home browser to homebuyer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Buying a home can be an intimidating process, with the biggest hurdle for many being coming up with enough funds for a down payment.

In a recent development, many people believe they need to put down at least 20% if they want a home. But that's not necessarily true.

Most buyers have down payments ranging from 3.5% to 20% of the sale price of the home they're buying, and there are many down payment assistance programs that can help aspiring homeowners pivot from home browser to homebuyer.

These programs can help buyers snag a home by providing cash that can go toward a down payment. There are even loan programs for certain qualified buyers that don't require any down payments. The array of offerings from federal, local, and private sources can take the form of looser loan requirements, outright grants of money, or tax credits, all of which make homeownership more affordable.

First-time homebuyers, often with certain qualifications, are often beneficiaries of the assistance. Lower-income buyers, those who serve in the military or are veterans, and those who purchase fixer-uppers or homes in rural areas might also be eligible for the help.

The assistance ranges greatly, from a grant of several thousand dollars to, at the high end, a savings of five figures over the life of the loan.

Down payment assistance can take several forms and can even help buyers circumvent the PMI payment.

Recent findings suggest that while 20% down has been something of a gold standard for homebuyers, it's also the minimum that generally lets them avoid private mortgage insurance, or PMI, which is assessed because lenders believe the loan carries risk. This in turn raises the homebuyer’s monthly expenses.

Sources indicate that here's an example: PMI is typically 0.5% to 1% of the loan amount per year. So if buyers put down less than 20% and their mortgage is $300,000, their PMI would be between $1,500 and $3,000 per year. That would add about $125 to $250 per month on top of their mortgage payment, a significant charge. (Homeowners can have PMI canceled when the equity in their home surpasses 20%.).

So, while a buyer can also choose loans that require a down payment of just a single digit, that PMI can stretch a budget paper-thin. That's where down payment assistance can help.

Sources indicate that at least 2,000 such programs exist across the country. Some are federal, but most tend to be at state and local levels, which is important to know when searching for help. Private organizations, from lenders to nonprofits, also work with borrowers who need help.

These programs might offer grants, loans, tax credits, or a combination of a couple of these benefits. Funding can come from our government, nonprofits, and private enterprises. Let’s take a closer look:.

Industry observers note that grants might be the most desirable form of down payment assistance. Typically, a grant is fully forgiven at closing and never has to be paid back. Yes, we’re talking about free money!

About 7% of down payment help comes in the form of grants, claims Veronica Khandelwal, vice president of HFA Relations at Down Payment Resource, which provides consumers with guidance on this kind of assistance. But there is a catch.

Sources indicate that “Grants require owner occupancy," she notes of the requirement for buyers to live in these properties. That's to make sure these loans don't go to investors or vacation-home buyers. "Some programs allow grants to be applied to multifamily purchases of one to four units so long as one of the units is occupied by the borrower.".

Forgivable loans are another option. These loans need to be repaid only if a repayment trigger event occurs, such as the home being sold before the end of the term, the home being no longer owner-occupied, the title being transferred, or the loan being defaulted on.

Industry observers note that deferred-payment loans are also available. These are paid back either at the end of the loan term or if a repayment trigger occurs. So, while it’s not a gift, it will help homebuyers get over that down payment hurdle and buy a house they might otherwise not have been able to afford.

Repayable loans are another leg up on homeownership. They require borrowers to make monthly payments, like a typical loan. But here's the good part: They do so at interest rates starting as low as 0%. That helps spread the down payment and closing costs over a number of years, making it much easier to enter the housing market.

Some agencies also offer a combination of these forms of assistance. That could mean that a portion of the help will be forgiven (or “written off” with no repayment needed), while some will need to be repaid. Tax credits are sometimes offered as well, further sweetening the deal.

Each down payment assistance program will have its own rules and guidelines, but the vast majority are offered only for a home that buyers will live in as a primary residence.

Here are some of the more popular national options folks might access to help them to pivot from home shopper to homebuyer.

FHA (Federal Housing Authority) loans were created by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development for first-time homeowners (HUD). These mortgages allow as little as 3.5% for the down payment, provided buyers have a credit score of 580 or higher, along with other qualifying factors. The federal government insures these loans, and for that reason, banks are more willing to loan money to homebuyers who have neither top-tier credit nor loads of cash to put down on the purchase.

FHA Section 203(k) loans require only 3% down, provided qualifying buyers will live in the property, typically one that needs work, while they fix it up. For buyers hoping for a DIY route into a dream home, this could be a win-win. The cost of improvements is included in the loan so buyers can finance both the home and up to $35,000 in repairs.

But buyers beware: The cost of materials and construction labor has spiked since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, and work is taking much longer to be completed than ever before.

Industry observers note that VA (U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs) loans might be offered directly by the VA or backed by the department. Several factors are considered, such as service history, duty status, income, and credit rating. But those who qualify can purchase a home with zero down as long as the sales price isn’t higher than the home’s appraised value.

Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac are federally funded loans that can help buyers skirt steep down payments. The Home Possible, HomeReady, and HomeOne loans typically offer a 3% down payment mortgage to qualifying, lower-income homebuyers.

In a recent development, good Neighbor Next Door is another HUD-sponsored program. In this case, law enforcement officers, teachers, firefighters, and emergency medical technicians can enjoy a substantial incentive in the form of a discount of 50% from the list price of the home in a community that is being revitalized. The buyer must live in the house for three years as a primary residence.

According to recent reports, teacher Next Door Grant is a program similar to the one above but is designed to help educators own their own homes. Grants to the tune of up to $8,000 in certain areas are possible with additional down payment assistance available in some circumstances.

Recent findings suggest that the USDA (U.S. Department of Agriculture) Rural Home Loan Program was created to assist people buying homes in rural locations. For qualifying, single-family properties, loans might be available with no money down. There are maximum income limits and other qualifications to be eligible for one of these mortgages.

There are plenty of other programs available as well. Different states and cities, as well as individual lenders and nonprofits, can help prospective homebuyers get the financing they need. Folks should put their location and "down payment assistance" into a search engine, and take a look at what's available. They might see everything from Habitat for Humanity to local religious organizations pop up. Also,visit Down Payment Resource.

One other path to explore is whether a buyer's job provides down payment assistance. A lot of employers may offer assistance in  the form of a $10,000 loan that is forgivable after five years.

Recent findings suggest that down payments hit a four-year low at the start of 2026. The median payment fell to $23,400 and 12.8% in Q1 2026, down 19% and 1.2 ppts year over year.

However, down payments remain well above pre-pandemic levels, as more buying is happening in the lower-down-payment South and Midwest, even as the Northeast stays deeply competitive.

The Northeast posted the highest median down payment at $57,600, reflecting higher home prices and more competition. The Northeast also sees the largest gap between what buyers are paying as a down payment today compared to pre-pandemic.

Compared to 2019, the Northeast has seen down payments climb 236.8%, significantly more than the next closest gap of 134.0% in the Midwest. These trends are consistent with the persistent upward pressure on home prices in these regions as scarce inventory is met with sustained buyer demand.

It has been revealed that get ready for some good news. There are a lot of misconceptions about who qualifies for down payment assistance.

“Many people think these programs are only available to low-income borrowers, first-time homebuyers, or for properties that have sales price limits,” indicates Down Payment Resource's Khandelwal. “But if you look, you’ll find specialized programs designed to assist specific groups, including first-generation homebuyers, minorities, Indigenous people, people of color, veterans, those with government jobs, disabilities, and more.”.

Here’s something else to smile about: A first-time homebuyer doesn't just mean someone who's never bought a home before.

Industry observers note that the federal government generally holds a broader definition of a first-time homebuyer. It’s someone who has not been a homeowner in the past three years. If you sold a house three-and-a-half years ago, you qualify as first-time buyer.

Buyers can take several different steps to find a down payment assistance program that’s right for them.

Check the federal programs mentioned above (like HUD, VA, USDA, Fannie Mae, and Freddie Mac), and see if there’s anything suitable.

It has been revealed that buyers should also visit their state’s Department of Housing website and see what might be listed, or call their number and inquire what down payment assistance programs might be available. Cities, towns, private lenders, and nonprofits may also have help.

“Homebuyers should seek the assistance of a mortgage lender who specializes in affordable lending to identify their best options,” advises Khandelwal.

Industry observers note that in terms of what is typically needed to access aid, the documentation is very much in line with what’s needed to apply for any mortgage. Buyers will likely need the following:.

Pay stubs plus W-2s from the past few years to verify employment and income history.

Any 1099 forms showing other income.

Details on the property they intend to buy (The real estate agent can share this information.).

The paperwork is processed in much the same way as a home loan, and there may be requests for more documents.

Then, if buyers are approved, they will be ready to move ahead with a lower—or no—down payment as their homeownership journey unfolds.

Janet Siroto is a journalist, editor, and trend tracker. Her work has appeared in Cosmopolitan, Good Housekeeping, and other publications.

Tech Report: F1 Finally Hiring Permanent Race Stewards, Replacing Volunteer Officials

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that unlike the typical ball sports, a significant number of on-track rule infractions are strictly tied to a specific penalty.
  • Sources indicate that the transition to full-time professional officials likely won't be completed by the start of the 2027 season.
  • In a recent development, "This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to delivering the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that unlike the typical ball sports, a significant number of on-track rule infractions are strictly tied to a specific penalty. The punishment is selected from a set range by part-time volunteers who are often criticized by drivers, teams and fans for their inconsistency. The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile confirmed on Thursday that it will be introducing full-time stewards to officiate Formula 1 next season. The sport's global governing body is finally shedding one of the last vestiges of its aristocratic past, aiming to provide more consistent rule calls. Welcome to 21st century, F1.

Sources indicate that the transition to full-time professional officials likely won't be completed by the start of the 2027 season. The FIA stated it's establishing a department of 12 to 15 full-time stewards recruited from its existing pool of international stewards. While they will initially complement the current part-timers, the role of the permanent stewards will expand as their roster grows. Beyond officiating F1 race weekends, the full-timers will form a constant rule-decision base and train their eventual successors with those precedents. FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem said:.

In a recent development, "This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to delivering the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport. The recruitment of full-time stewards is a significant step in our longstanding mission of building a dedicated officiating ecosystem in the FIA Formula One World Championship, it is also an investment in the future of our sport.".

It has been revealed that formula 1 was formed in the same aristocratic primordial pool of international sports that encouraged the International Olympic Committee to ban professional athletes until 1986. European aristocrats held the reins of international motorsport until that same period. Prince Paul Alfons von Metternich-Winneburg finished a decade as FIA President in 1985. If the Metternich name sounds familiar, he was a great-grandson of Prince Klemens von Metternich, the influential 19th-century Austrian statesman.

While F1 has become a multi-billion-dollar enterprise, the championship's officiating has long remained locked in an era when amateurism was a virtue. As a result, the F1 stewards' office is filled with people who can afford to spend significant time and money earning the prerequisite credentials and gaining the necessary experience officiating smaller events. The unpaid volunteers are often successful lawyers and automotive executives, sometimes employed by companies directly involved in F1. Thankfully, those days are finally coming to an end.

US to install 36% more wind turbines in 2025 than previous year

📅 18 Dec 2025 | ⏱️ 4 min read (751 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Windpowerengineering

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the United States is expected to add more than 7 GW of wind installations in 2025, a 36% increase over the previous year, and the five-year outlook remains unchanged quarter-over-quarter from previous forecast, according to the “U.S.
  • Sources indicate that amid a challenging market environment, the report demonstrates that the United States is on track to add 46 GW of newly introduced wind capacity from 2025 to 2029, with total projected volumes unchanged quarter-on-quarter from previous forecasts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the United States is expected to add more than 7 GW of wind installations in 2025, a 36% increase over the previous year, and the five-year outlook remains unchanged quarter-over-quarter from previous forecast, according to the “U.S. Wind Energy Monitor” report released by Wood Mackenzie and the American Clean Power Association (ACP).

Sources indicate that amid a challenging market environment, the report demonstrates that the United States is on track to add 46 GW of newly introduced wind capacity from 2025 to 2029, with total projected volumes unchanged quarter-on-quarter from previous forecasts. However, timing has shifted, as 2026 and 2027 will deliver significant gains, at 10.7 GW and 12.7 GW, respectively, as more assets advance through the development pipeline.

While Q3 installations came in 23% below forecast at 932 MW, the market has shown progress with 3.8 GW queued for Q4 2025 — representing 52% of the year’s total expected capacity. This back-loaded installation pattern is consistent with typical project-commissioning timelines.

U.S. turbine order intake has rebounded to pre-One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) levels quarter-over-quarter, supported by 2+ GW of firm commitments in Q3, the biggest intake in the region in the last nine months and a 79% quarter-over-quarter increase. However, true visibility remains limited as OEMs increasingly withhold project details and much qualifying “start-of-construction” activity occurs through off-site component manufacturing.

The market will then see a noticeable drop off, as 2029 weakens meaningfully quarter-over-quarter following project cancellations and inactive designations for late-decade capacity, driven by permitting and broader development challenges.

According to recent reports, “The U.S. power market is facing mounting strain after a decade of flat demand, with utilities committing to 160 GW of large-load additions. This represents a significant opportunity for wind energy, which benefits from strengthened economic fundamentals and a compelling business case driven by its competitively low LCOE,” said Leila Garcia da Fonseca, director of research at Wood Mackenzie. “However, turbine costs remain elevated due to tariffs and mid-term wind growth will depend on resolving permitting and policy uncertainty.”.

According to recent reports, power demand growth through 2029 is expected to average around 3% compared to just 0.7% over the previous decade, with data centers accounting for approximately 59 GW of the 90 GW total peak demand growth. This surge in baseload demand positions wind as a natural fit to meet rising power needs.

In a recent development, the five-year capacity outlook remains unchanged at 39.8 GW of added capacity quarter-over-quarter. The 2025-2027 pipeline is fully committed with all projects having turbine orders in place. More than 60% of the three-year capacity outlook has been commissioned or is under construction.

Activity is led by western states, such as Wyoming, New Mexico and others, that will account for 34% of activity in this time period. Major projects driving the outlook include Pattern’s 3.5-GW SunZia project in New Mexico, which will position the developer as 2026’s top installer, and Invenergy’s 998-MW Towner Energy Center in Colorado, the largest single project expected in 2027.

The market continues expanding geographically, with Arkansas bringing its first utility-scale onshore wind project online through Cordelio’s Crossover Wind.

The repowering market remains strong, as Wood Mackenzie projects that 18 projects will drive 2.5 GW of capacity additions in the next three years.

Recent findings suggest that wood Mackenzie expects the offshore installation pace to slow in Q4 2025 due to harsh winter weather conditions, pushing remaining capacity into 2026. Despite these near-term adjustments, Vineyard Wind has demonstrated strong execution, connecting 15 turbines in Q3 and delivering 200 GWh through nine months.

“U.S. offshore wind indicates diverging momentum,” said Garcia Da Fonseca. “Projects under construction with COD estimated for 2026 continue to hit key milestones, but post-2027 developments face potential delays amid constrained wind turbine installation vessel capacity, driving delays and contract terminations.”.

The offshore sector is also experiencing significant financial pressure.

The report highlights that uncertainty around tariffs is a threat to projections. Wood Mackenzie projects that tariffs will drive up turbine costs in 2026, before moderating in subsequent years. In total, U.S. onshore wind capex is projected to increase by 5% through 2029.

It has been revealed that “U.S. wind turbine pricing is experiencing unprecedented uncertainty as conflicting market and regulatory forces interact,” noted Garcia Da Fonseca. “Domestic manufacturing overcapacity relative to permitted project volumes, particularly after 2028, would normally place downward pressure on prices. Despite this, onshore wind costs are expected to continue rising due to tariff exposure on raw material inputs and subcomponents.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when Mercedes introduced the seventh-generation R232 SL roadster, it was only offered in performance-oriented AMG trims, with an ultra-luxury Maybach variant coming a few years later. For the first time in the model's history, a Benz-branded SL was missing from the lineup, but that's about to change because of buyer feedback. Some folks apparently miss the subdued, grand touring nature that SLs of old provided, and they don't all have the $230,000 it takes to enter Maybach land, so a Mercedes-Benz SL is coming back.

In a recent development, with this current generation, Mercedes wanted to bring the SL and AMG GT Coupe closer together, and it seems that may have been a slight miscalculation on the German automaker's part. While big power and big prices are all well and good, it's not exactly what the average SL owner is looking for — especially when the Mercedes-AMG GT Coupe exists, according to Autocar. They missed some of the refinement and long-distance cruising ability of the old cars. Basically, the new one was hurting their agining backs.

Now that its mid-cycle refresh time, the GT will remain the performance-oriented vehicle, and the SL will take on a more relaxed demeaner, CEO Ola Källenius told Autocar. It'll trade in rock hard suspension and track times for comfort and ride quality. The two vehicles will also get revised engines to meet newly introduced emissions standards in Communist Europe.

Mercedes will discontinue the entry-level SL43 and GT43 that use a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-4, and the same fate will befall the SL63 S E Performance and its 805-horsepower plug-in-hybrid V8 powertrain. Instead, the updated SLs will all get 48-volt mild-hybrid systems, and the fresh entry-level engine is expected to be a 443-hp turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-6, which is far more befitting of a grand tourer anyway. That model will probably be called SL500, while an SL580 will have the new M177 Evo flat-plane crank V8 we first saw in the refreshed S-Class.

Don't worry, drop-top AMG fans. The AMG SL isn't going anywhere, even if the E Performance is. Autocar speculates that the M177 will be also used in an SL63 that'll put out a notch over 600 horsepower, which should be more than enough for the folks who are into things of that nature. (The AMG SL55 will effectively be replaced by the V8 Benz SL580.).

It has been revealed that it's not just an ethos change, either. Mercedes notes the Benz SL will have front-end styling that alighes closer with the standard Mercedes look, with a simpler grille that has one horizontal bar across it rather than the more aggressive AMG grille with all its vertical canes. It'll also make use of the latest Digital Light headlight system from the firm, which, of course, features three-pointed-star daytime running lights. Inside, the car will get an upgraded MB.OS platform to run the infotainment and the rest of the car's brain as well as some latest physical control.

If this all sounds exciting to you in a way that the AMG SL didn't, well, you've got to hold on just a little bit longer. Källenius indicates the refreshed SL, which is going to be "more of a Mercedes-Benz," is expected to lauch in 2027.

From smarter waterproofing to 360-degree rail adjustment, Top Rack Technology is putting installer efficiency, rooftop flexibility, and cost control at the center of its latest product lineup.

Recent findings suggest that as the solar industry continues to look for ways to reduce installation costs and streamline residential projects, mounting hardware is getting a fresh dose of innovation. Top Rack Technology, Inc. (TRT) is making that case at RE+ 2026, where the solar racking manufacturer is showcasing six new mounting solutions designed to simplify rooftop installations, improve flexibility, and help installers work more efficiently.

Its latest lineup reflects a practical approach to product development: addressing everyday installation challenges while keeping system performance, aesthetics, and affordability in focus.

Six Products, One Common Goal: Better Installation Efficiency.

Industry observers note that among the new offerings is TRT’s Full-Coverage Skirt System, which targets an notable consideration in residential solar: appearance. By concealing exposed array edges, the system delivers a cleaner, more finished look that can help installations better complement residential properties.

The new TRT-G2 Bracket takes aim at installation simplicity and competitive pricing. Designed around practical field requirements, the bracket can be paired with TRT’s ButyLok waterproofing component, creating an integrated attachment and roof-sealing solution.

It has been revealed that waterproofing is particularly important in rooftop solar, where roof penetrations are still a critical consideration for installers and property owners alike. ButyLok introduces a shoe-like component containing pre-applied, gel-like butyl material. When compressed by the G2 bracket, the material spreads across the intended sealing surface, potentially reducing manual sealant application and simplifying the installation process.

Sources indicate that TRT is also introducing SAVRIX, another residential attachment option developed with manufacturing efficiency, installation practicality, and cost competitiveness top of mind.. Meanwhile, the RF-2 Rail Fastener is designed to simplify rail-to-bracket connections.

Top Rack Technology’s FreePivot Bracket features a 360-degree rotatable rail fastener and built-in height adjustment to accommodate varying rooftop conditions and simplify solar panel installations. Credit: Top Rack Technology.

But perhaps the most versatile addition is the FreePivot Bracket. Its 360-degree rotatable rail fastener allows installers to accommodate attachment points that aren’t perfectly aligned. Built-in height adjustment helps compensate for uneven roof surfaces, while its all-metal construction supports durability. The one-orientation design and single-socket installation concept are also intended to reduce tool changes and keep crews moving.

Hardware Meets Digital Project Planning.

Beyond the six new products, TRT is showcasing its established portfolio, including the TRT 01 Rail-less Base System, TRT 02 Rail-Base System, and TRT 03 Tile Hook System.

The company is also highlighting its Online BOM Design Tool, which supports project setup, structural design inputs, module layouts, engineering verification, and automated bill-of-materials generation. Connecting digital planning with physical mounting solutions could offer installers and distributors a more streamlined path from project design to field execution.

Recent findings suggest that installation hardware doesn’t need to be flashy to make a difference. Improvements in attachment flexibility, waterproofing, assembly time, and aesthetics can translate into meaningful operational advantages.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elle and Dakota Fanning have been in the spotlight for decades, but their upcoming project, “The Nightingale,” marks the first time they’ve played sisters onscreen—an experience that brought them “closer” together, both on set and at home.

While they’ve visited each other on set in the past and even separately played different versions of the same character in the 2001 film “I Am Sam,” Elle, 28, told Vanity Fair that actually working with each other is a totally different ball game.

In a recent development, “It certainly brought us closer, which was hard to imagine—to be closer,” she stated. “Our mom always left us little notes in suitcases, like, ‘Just savor this time together. This is precious.’”.

Dakota, 32, confirmed that they took their mother’s advice.

“We did really savor it,” she said. “And the biggest takeaway for me is when we have each other and when we’re together, we can do anything. That’s really how I feel. There’s nothing that I couldn’t do with Elle there with me.”.

Industry observers note that that noted, the job wasn’t easy. The Fannings traveled to Budapest to shoot on location, where they lived together.

“It was a challenging shoot, not going to lie. It was physically tiring, certainly emotionally taxing,” noted Elle.

After a long day of using lots of “brain power” on set, the sisters had to find a way to “recharge” each evening.

For Dakota and Elle, that meant eating lots of Thai food and streaming “The Real Housewives,” true crime, and “Margo’s Got Money Troubles”—the TV series the younger sister stars in, which was released while they filmed “The Nightingale.”.

Dakota revealed that on a day off, she’d often find herself cleaning up after Elle, which was poetic as her character, Vianne, also tidies her sister Isabelle’s mess.

“Her bed in the mornings is like a tornado has run through it,” she stated. “She’s just one of those sleepers. It’s all twisted into a crazy thing. I was like, ‘That’s no fun to get into a bed that’s all crumpled and rumpled. Let me make it nice.’”.

The older sister stated that “it became a routine,” and she “always made her bed like that” when possible.

Elle said, “It’s art imitating life, because there’s even a scene where Vianne is making Isabelle’s bed, too.”.

According to recent reports, dakota and Elle were born in Conyers, GA. As young girls, they traveled between the Atlanta suburb and Los Angeles to work before relocating to the West Coast full time.

“When we were younger, we wanted to make sure that people saw us differently, and we wanted to give each other space to carve our own path,” Elle told Vanity Fair in 2025. “But as adults, it’s been very fulfilling to merge.”.

One of the most major ways the sisters have merged their lives in adulthood was in 2017, when they purchased a gorgeous $2.3 million property together.

According to Architectural Digest, they lived in a Cape Cod-style home in the Valley Village area of San Fernando Valley.

The 4,550-square-foot residence was perched at the end of a private, gated driveway and had a very classic aesthetic with white rose bushes planted along the front walkway.

The interiors were defined by delicate details, such as baby blue brocade-patterned walls, intricate chandeliers, and coffered ceilings.

The sisters sold the six-bedroom, six-bathroom estate for just under $2.7 million in May 2020.

It’s clear that Dakota was a fan of the dwelling’s traditional style, as she bought a very similar-looking home in Toluca Lake for $2.95 million in 2019, just before offloading the property she shared with Elle.

According to Architectural Digest, Dakota’s newer home spans 4,428 square feet and boasts five bedrooms and six bathrooms. It’s flooded with natural light and, like the first home, has crystal chandeliers, a pool in the backyard, and a double-height entry hall.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that friends, I'm going to give you a little peek behind the curtain at how this, your most beloved weekly automotive column, works. It goes like this: I find a bunch of car listings, and then I write a couple thousand words about them. You might expect the former to be the fun part, browsing all week for upcoming and interesting listings, but it's actually the back half I really enjoy. See, finding listings has a problem: Eventually, things get old.

Industry observers note that that's why you need gimmicks. Cars from a certain area, cars with a certain theme, cars from history's greatest cinematic achievement. Today, the gimmick is price: A hard cap of $5,000, which no vehicle exceeds. I honestly expected a bunch of beige commuter cars in questionable stated of repair, but I'm shocked at how good the offerings were in rust-free states. We've got Benzes, BMWs, and bikes as far as the eye can see. Welcome, my friends, to a budget-conscious edition of the week's Dopest Cars.

Sources indicate that remember when nice FR-Ses or BRZs cost five figures? Well, they still do. This example is no one's definition of immaculate, but it should be everyone's definition of a deal. This is Miata money! Less than Miata money! For under five grand, you could have one of the best-handling chassis out there, and with an engine that's not even blown! Yet. Probably.

Even if/when that does happen, $5,000 leaves plenty of room in the budget for something new to go under that theoretically carbon hood. K-swap, 2JZ, RB26, LS, EJ257, everything fits. Do whatever you want forever with this car, because it's up for whatever. You can fit anything between those front wheels, and you should. Do something cool with it, then reach out to me and send me pictures and videos of the cool thing you did. I'll write about it. That's an Amber promise. (Amber does not get to make these promises. -Ed).

Not only is there a new liquid-cooled replacement for this old 411cc Himalayan out there, in the form of the Himalayan 450, but there's now a bigger brother in Enfield's adventure lineup with the Himi 750. This is neither of those, but they're still relevant here because their very existence makes the first-generation Himalayan cheaper by comparison. It's slower, less powerful, and altogether not as advanced a bike — perfect for those of you looking to get started with something approachable.

Personally, I see the appeal in a dead-simply little ADV like the Himalayan 411. There's so little to go wrong, it's the kind of adventure bike that you can actually really adventure with. Sure, service intervals aren't Honda long, but good luck getting an Africa Twin for three grand. The Himalayan won't get you anywhere fast, it won't be the most stylish way around, but it'll certainly get you where you're going.

It has been revealed that yeah, I was surprised too. A Z32 300ZX, in seemingly good shape, for under $5,000. Are cars just free in the states where they don't rust away into dust after two winters? Do you Arizonans just have your pick of any cool car you want for approximately the price of a Costco hot dog? Don't tell me. I can't bear to know.

It has been revealed that anyway, this 300ZX isn't perfect, so at least I can take some solace in that while I scroll my locally-available rustbuckets and cry myself to sleep. It needs a whole wheel bearing, something that's surely a pain to replace on a completely rust-free car where none of the undercarriage bolts have fused to each other and become one piece of metal that's inseparable no matter how much heat and torque you apply. Surely that's the case. Please just let me have this one. Not even this car, just this dream of perfect-car availability outside my region.

Pink R6! Well, pinkish gray. It's pinker than any factory fairings for the bike, at least. Actually, none of you are allowed to buy this one, I want it for myself once I win a quick Powerball. Just keep scrolling to the next slide.

According to recent reports, mister Two? More like mister too expensive, except in Southern California where these can apparently be had for $4,500. I see why so many car and bike people live there, with the beautiful roads and temperate climate and availability of cars that aren't just piled of rust with a VIN. I get the appeal, but unfortunately I can never join you all. If I spend more than five days in LA I start to go mad due to lack of walkable infrastructure.

Anyway, MR2. This one's not a turbo car, but that doesn't really matter for this kind of money. It also has a beat-up body kit, but again I don't really care. In fact, I prefer a car that has a couple dents, dings, and battle scars — it wears its story on its body panels. This isn't a garage queen, it's a car that's really been used the way its engineers and designers intended. That's worth celebrating, and each rock scratch and bit of drift stitching is a celebration in itself.

Are people over 240Ds now? Have they all moved on to J80 Land Cruisers or something? Back in my day, a 240D in this kind of condition for this kind of money would barely last a day on Marketplace or Craigslist, let alone the weeks this one's been on the market. I know, it's not a wagon, but still. It's not gasoline either!

According to recent reports, the seller of this particular 240 claims that it not only runs and drives, but has a fairly considerable amount of work done under the hood. The battery, starter, glow plugs, injectors, and fluids are all latest. There's also some unspecified "work" on the head, which probably doesn't mean it's been overheated and warped at some point in its history. I'd bet that didn't happen. How would you even overheat a dependable old Volvo diesel like that, even if you wanted to? These things are so bulletproof.

Not every sub-$5,000 car on Facebook Marketplace is an enthusiast icon. I accept that. That doesn't mean that the remainder have to be bad, though — they can be beloved commuter cars with more sporting pretensions than they really need, like this Mazda3. It's no MazdaSpeed, sure, but it's a stick-shift compact sedan with Mazda's jinba ittai philosophy behind its chassis, engine, and suspension design. I think that's pretty good.

This one seems to be in good shape, and the seller certainly claims the same, though it's a little tough to tell what exactly is going on in the photos. They're so smudged, or blurry, or streaked with sun — I can't even tell why they're wrong, I just know that they are. It's still a good car, but damn, Marketplace sellers. Step your photography game up. Or, at least, wipe your phone camera on your shirt before you take your listing photos.

In a recent development, there's been a Prelude parked outside my girlfriend's apartment for a few weeks now, and it looks a lot like this one. Red, not white, but in a similar state of aged-yet-solid — not the cleanest, not the stock-est, but still more than drivable. Well, I assume it's drivable, but it hasn't moved for street sweeping in a while. I hope it's drivable.

It has been revealed that this Prelude not only drives, but ought to drive pretty well — it's an Si model, after all. The seller claims it's "mechanically pristine" but that the interior needs work, though it looks perfect inside and out to my eye. Maybe I just have lower standards for my car interiors, but this one looks great. All I can see is a bit of work heeded on the sunroof shade, and what might be the tiniest rip in the side of the driver's seat. I don't think either of those are worth addressing with anything more than a bit of gaffer's tape, honestly.

Hey, it's my old bike! Not exactly, mine was a better color, but I did ride a G 310 GS when I first moved to Newly introduced York and started working at the good ship Jalopnik. I maintain that a baby ADV is secretly the best way to get started on two wheels, provided you're tall enough to manage the seat height —  they can do a bit of everything, and they'll help you figure out where you want to spend your two-wheel time. Try it all on a small adventure bike, then see what you like doing best and cater your next bike towards that.

In a recent development, this particular G 310 GS, though, has one benefit over mine: It's much cheaper. I sold mine for something like $6,000, and this one's asking just $4,000 — surely you can talk the seller down from that. Imagine picking this bike up for a cool $3,500! You'd have a fantastic beginner bike. I got almost too comfortable on mine, riding it sidesaddle and one-legged through Brooklyn traffic, and you could get that same level of comfort on two wheels.

It has been revealed that C'mon, I don't need to sell you on this one. A Suzuki Sidekick for under $2,000! Just go buy it.

Way Before Ducati's Desmo, The Tech giant Started With Puppies

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (686 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are few pairings in the motorcycle world more notable than Ducati and Desmo.
  • Recent findings suggest that in the midst of World War II, before Vespa began selling its own purpose-built machines to the Italian public to get the country back on the road, Ducati was already in the throes of doing the same.
  • Hearing the "puppy" in action, it doesn't sound much like a puppy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are few pairings in the motorcycle world more notable than Ducati and Desmo. The famed Italian manufacturer is known for making some of the most desirably fast bikes, and so happens to be leading the MotoGP World Championship as of this writing. None of that would be possible, if it weren't for the company's puppies — or rather its Cucciolo engines.

Recent findings suggest that in the midst of World War II, before Vespa began selling its own purpose-built machines to the Italian public to get the country back on the road, Ducati was already in the throes of doing the same. At this time, Ducati was known for its machining and radios, but had decided to try its hand at making an engine. It created a tiny prototype four-stroke cycle engine, paired with a little two-speed gearbox, intended to be affixed to a bicycle to simply give riders a boost of power. The engine's supposed barking-like noise helped inspire its name, Cucciolo, which in Italian means "puppy.".

Hearing the "puppy" in action, it doesn't sound much like a puppy. Although the engines demonstrated in these running videos are upwards of 60-80 years old, so they sound like old puppies.

Sources indicate that according to Ducati's history, the original Siata factory where the Cucciolo was made had been damaged in the war, and a new factory would open in 1945 to get production rolling. Siata, lastly known as Societa Italiana Applicazioni Tecniche Auto-Aviatorie, did make automobiles, and was tapped to produce Ducati's Cucciolos. In just months demand had outpaced Siata's production capabilities, making at least 240 engines a day, and Ducati moved to take on manufacturing itself.

The Cucciolo would go through three different iterations of the engine, the T2 was a sportier version that had an output of nearly 2 hp and could reach top speeds upwards of 37 mph. The T3 arrived in 1948, featuring a three-speed gearbox. Molto bene!

According to recent reports, all of these engines were meant to be installed and mounted onto other bicycles, but Ducati began to see the benefits of doing the same in-house. In 1949, Ducati worked with the airplane manufacturer Caproni to make a tube frame, that could then be paired with the Cucciolo T3 for Ducati's first fully produced motorized bike. Yet the Italian brand's first true complete motorcycle would be the Ducati 60, rolled out in 1950. It's tiny 60cc engine was another step towards Ducati's famed motorcycle history. Power output was rated for 2 hp at 4500 rpm, with the bike weighing in at 100 pounds. Of course, much like Vespa and Piaggio, Ducati wasted no time in getting into racing and entered its 60 into competition.

Recent findings suggest that production of Cucciolo engines didn't cease with the making of the 60, but the manufacturing may have changed hands. This 1953 Ducati Cucciolo Rocher Mark IV, on auction with Iconic Motorbikes, was built a few years after the introduction of the Ducati 60. Ducati at this point had allowed other companies to makes its engines, but the Ducati and Cucciolo names remained.

Iconic's particular example was made by Rocher, who according to the auction site, had "built high-end cyclomotors with unique and often extravagant designs. They manufactured Ducati Cucciolo engines with the best materials and cast parts in aluminum rather than using Ducati's inferior high silicon content alloys. This means that damage to Rocher engines can be repaired through welding, which is not possible with Ducati's engines." The switch on Rocher's part makes for an amusing reminder of Ducati's reputation of having engines some individuals believe are difficult to maintain, i.e. the notorious Desmo jokes.

Sources indicate that just a few years after the 60 was created, in 1956, Ducati introduced its first desmodromic valvetrain by putting it into a 125 Grand Prix racing motorcycle. Today its unique but endearing build is featured on many of Ducati's bikes, including most recently, its newly minted motocross bikes. Yet these impressive chariots of speed and the notorious Desmo wouldn't be here, had it not been for the original "puppy.".

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

20 Official James Bond Cars Ranked From Most Famous To Most Obscure

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2274 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that amazon MGM Studios is in charge of the new tack the longstanding James Bond franchise will take, after paying $1 billion to the Broccoli family for creative control last year.
  • And surely there will be a new car for Bond to drive around looking cool.
  • While we don't yet know what car Pattinson, Robert Pattinson will be driving as 007, we can spend the next couple of years or more dreaming up what might make for a good Bond car in 2029 or 2030.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that amazon MGM Studios is in charge of the new tack the longstanding James Bond franchise will take, after paying $1 billion to the Broccoli family for creative control last year. And that comes after spending $8.5 billion in 2022 on the MGM Studios merger, which garnered the Bezos manufacturer control of Bond's back catalog and intellectual property. Amazon has tasked Oscar-nominated director Denis Villeneuve with helming the next Bond film, and this week signed actor Robert Pattinson as the new face of the franchise.

And surely there will be a new car for Bond to drive around looking cool. Maybe, if we're lucky, he'll have an extensive desert chase sequence through the Sahara or something, and he can take a Q-modified version of Aston Martin's new Dakar race car for a spin.

While we don't yet know what car Pattinson, Robert Pattinson will be driving as 007, we can spend the next couple of years or more dreaming up what might make for a good Bond car in 2029 or 2030. He famously drove a trio of Volvos in the Twilight series, running a C30, an XC60, and an S60 R-design. What else has Pattinson driven on-screen? Oh, nothing special, just the frickin' Batmobile!

Sources indicate that while we don't know what the future Bond will drive, we can take a look at Bond cars of the past and judge them on their merits. Some are much better than others, of course. I'm going to put them in order of most to least famous, and we can argue about it in the comments. Let me know what you think and tell me why I'm wrong.

Industry observers note that amidst the 1977 baddies-chasing-Bond action scene in the Roger Moore era's "The Spy Who Loved Me," James Bond adeptly dispatches a motorcycle, a car full of baddies (including Richard Kiel's Jaws), and a helicopter in the Italian countryside. Bond's heavily modified Lotus Esprit takes the chase underwater, surprising his passenger-seat companion, KGB agent Maj. Anya Amasova (Triple X, aka Barbara Bach).

According to recent reports, the Lotus had just launched to the public a year earlier, bringing hard-edged "folded paper" Giorgetto Giugiaro design and a 160-horsepower Type 907 2-liter four-cylinder engine to the street. The 2,200-pound Lotus was praised in its day for great handling and steering, the motoring press considered it underpowered. As far as I'm aware, however, Lotus did not build any submersible Esprits — that was all the doing of MI6's Q Branch.

In a recent development, once at sea, the Lotus tucked away its wheels and sprouted fins and a periscope. With the press of a button, Bond rolled out a torpedo straight upward at the hovering helicopter, blowing it to bits. This chase sequence seems a bit staid and underwhelming in 2026, but back in the late 1970s, it was positively the state of the art of action sequencing.

Industry observers note that while many might argue that Bond is synonymous with a silver Aston Martin, the character has had so many different ones over the years that they all kind of blend together. He's driven lots of non-Astons, too! The submersible Lotus is, if you ask me, the one that is most easily identifiable as a specific Bond car, making it my choice for the most famous individual example. Feel free to let me know why you think I'm wrong.

The iconic Aston Martin DB5 has been a pretty consistent piece of James Bond lore for decades. Co-starring more often than any other car, the DB5 has appeared in eight franchise films. Across the recent Daniel Craig series of Bond films, the DB5 made recurring guest spots in Bond's garage in "Casino Royale," "Skyfall," "Spectre," and "No Time To Die." It also co-starred with Pierce Brosnan in "GoldenEye" and "Tomorrow Never Dies." The car is perhaps most famous for its screen time in 1964's "Goldfinger" and 1965's "Thunderball," alongside Sean Connery's Bond.

In a recent development, "Goldfinger" set the standard for Bond cars, as it was the first time gadgets had been fitted. This car had an ejector seat, machine guns hidden behind the front turn-signal lamps, a rotating license plate display, rear-deployed smoke screen and oil slick, a bulletproof rear window screen, wheel blades for slashing tires, and an onboard homing system.

When most people think about James Bond, they think of shaken dry martinis, Omega watches, a Walther PPK compact semi-automatic pistol, and a silver Aston Martin. The Aston is iconic, but perhaps because it is so subdued in its appearance, and because all of the individual Astons blend together in the zeitgeist, it isn't quite as famous as the Lotus.

In a recent development, an argument could certainly be made for the DB5 as the best-known Bond car, but the DB5 never went underwater, did it? In this case, I think the Lotus wins just for the cool factor, but it's a narrow victory. And perhaps a pyrrhic one, as Bond never again helmed a Lotus for a film. Aston has been with Bond for decades, and I'd be surprised if Pattinbond drives anything from another manufacturer.

Bond has also driven a DBS in "On Her Majesty's Secret Service,"  a V8 Vantage in 1987's "The Living Daylights," a V12 Vanquish in "Die Another Day," a modern DBS in "Casino Royale," a DB10 in "Spectre," and while he didn't drive it, Bond even had a Valhalla in "No Time To Die." About half of the films released have featured an Aston. It's hard to separate the character from the British manufacturer, by design. Aston has spent millions associating its products with the world's greatest spy.

It has been revealed that perhaps the most famous use of an Aston in recent Bond films was the chase scene in "Casino Royale" (above) which sees Bond driving, and then crashing, the then-newly introduced DBS revival. While running down baddies on a wet night road, Bond comes upon Eva Green's Vesper Lynd having been dumped in the middle of the road. To avoid her, Double-Oh-Seven manages to roll his car a then-Guinness-record seven times on-screen.

Aston hasn't been there for every Bond installment, and the relationship went dormant for some time. Since the Craig era of Bond began, Aston has been pumping up its connection with the franchise, promoting the tie-ins nearly as hard as it does now with its Formula 1 relationship. Because both parties seem to benefit from working together, it would take quite a lot of pull to separate them for future installments, I believe.

In a recent development, of course, since the franchise is now under fresh ownership, things might change. Maybe Amazon will want Bond to drive a Slate truck or Rivian instead. Pattinson, meanwhile, has a personal relationship with watchmaker Jaeger-LeCoultre, so perhaps his Bond also won't be wearing the iconic Omega. At this point, the future of what Bond is could be decided by Jeff Bezos himself.

For a brief moment during the Brosnan era, Britain's licensed-to-kill spook drove German cars. When Brosnan got the role, he was cast in "GoldenEye" alongside BMW's small Z3 sports car decked out with plenty of weapons. Unfortunately, it was little more than paid product placement and was off-screen as quickly as it came, seemingly just there for the minimum required contractual time.

It has been revealed that my favorite of the BondMWs was the long-wheelbase V12 7-series in "Tomorrow Never Dies." In an effort to thwart the baddies while maintaining his safety and security, Bond uses the car's fictional remote-control capabilities (with an Ericsson mobile phone trackpad!) to drive around from the rear seat. For years I wished I could do something similar with my own cars, despite it serving no purpose in my life. I'm not a spy, and I don't need to escape baddies (as far as you know), but it's cool nonetheless. This giant stately sedan met its end when Bond eventually drove it off a parking garage roof. I still want an E38-generation 7-series, just thinking about it now.

Industry observers note that I'm going to get some guff for this, but Brosnan's BMW Z8 in "The World Is Not Enough" is, was, and always will be the best-looking car Bond ever drove on-screen. Like the Z3, this incredible grand tourer didn't really get enough screen time. What little time it did have, however, it looked stunning, and met an incredibly satisfying end. After using a fender-mounted rocket launcher to take down a helicopter, a second helicopter fitted with tree-trimming saws sliced the Bimmer in half (pictured above)!

Recent findings suggest that it's unlikely we'll ever see Bond in a BMW again, and that's probably a good thing. Could you imagine him driving a new X6 M Competition? I shudder at the thought.

Recent findings suggest that the collective Jaguar and Land Rover brands have been important to the Bond franchise over the last few decades, having provided quite a few vehicles for bad guys and henchmen to make chase in across several films. As far as I can tell, Bond only ever drove one Jaguar, the State-provided long-wheelbase XJ that Craig uses to "kidnap" M and abscond to the Skyfall estate in an effort to stay one step ahead of Raoul Silva. The car is on-screen for just over a minute before the pair swap to Bond's personal Aston Martin DB5. There's a reason the Jag is so far down the list, of course, as he barely drives it, and there's very little action happening.

Despite Aston and Lotus handily smashing Jaguar on the cool factor when it comes to Bond cars, Jag's involvement as the car of choice for international baddies definitely ups the leaping cat's cool quotient a bit. Think back to "Die Another Day" and you'll have seen henchman Tang Lin Zao driving a bright green Jaguar XKR fitted with Bond-level gadgets, including grille rocket launchers, a minigun, and thermal imaging. It wasn't a match for Bond's invisible Aston Vanquish on ice, but it was still very cool to see.

Do you remember when wrestler-turned-actor Dave Bautista became a Bond villain in "Spectre"? Along with his brawn, Bautista also brought an eye-catching hypercar to the franchise with the Jaguar CX75 concept taking the fight to Bond's malfunctioning never-sold-to-the-public Aston DB10.

According to recent reports, both cars are absolutely spectacular to look at, but the chase is a little underwhelming. Bond eventually has to sink the Aston and use the ejector seat button to escape Bautista's character Hinx.

Recent findings suggest that you'd be forgiven for never really associating Bond with American cars, but he's definitely driven them a few times. Most of these scenes were filmed before I was born, in an era when Bond movies were much more camp than the nonstop action set pieces they are today. While the Bond books were always pretty interesting, the movies tended toward the absurd, particularly in the early days.

In what is perhaps the most nonsensical move in all of James Bond history, Roger Moore's "The Man with the Golden Gun" came with American Motors Corporation product placement and a "Dukes Of Hazzard"-style bridge jumping sequence. Bond steals a 1974 AMC Hornet X from a dealership in an effort to chase down the bad guy's AMC Matador. When he needs to cross a river and the bridge is out, Bond lines up and puts pedal to the metal, going for style points in the process. If you ask me, this scene could have done without the slide-whistle sound effect. The stunt was pretty stunning, however, as stunt performer extraordinaire Loren Willert managed the jump in one take (above).

I've lived in snowy winter climates all my life, and I'm not sure I've heard squealing tires quite like what happens in the Switzerland ice-racing sequence from "On Her Majesty's Secret Service." In spite of the bad use of Foley art in the sequence (and the poor Ford Escort that ends up on its roof), it remains one of my favorite old-school moments in a Bond film. Even better, it wasn't Bond driving at the time.

According to recent reports, call me crazy, but I think the cars Bond drives in the original Ian Fleming novels are significantly cooler than whatever Aston Martin he's driving this week. These are, sadly, the least famous of them all, because literacy is falling and regular reading is at its lowest level in decades. Please, go pick up a book, folks!

In the early books, namely "Casino Royale," "Live and Let Die," and "Moonraker," James Bond drives a 1930 4.5-liter Blower Bentley. While Bond's Bentley is mechanically identical to those driven by the Bentley Boys to Le Mans victory in the 1920s, his was painted battleship grey, while the racers were traditional British Racing Green. After a brief affair with a Bentley Mark IV Drophead Coupe, Bond settles on a supercharged Bentley Mark II Continental he calls "The Locomotive" that he maintains through the rest of the original 14-novel run.

Once John Gardner took over writing Bond novels in 1981, the character acquired the "Silver Beast," a Saab 900 Turbo, which he kept for much of the official book series run. Jalopnik has described the car as "the most obscure James Bond car of all time" and I can't help but agree with that sentiment 14 years later. With over 240 horsepower and a top speed of 170 miles per hour, it's a pretty rad little machine. Maybe, if we beg, Jeff Bezos will let the next Bond car be a highly modified 1980s Saab 900 Turbo.

Latest Update: Here's How The White Boxes On Traffic Lights Help Traffic Flow

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Even if you didn't agree to the Terms & Conditions, Massive Brother is surveilling you anyway.
  • Recent findings suggest that the good news is these white boxes are radar-based and relatively low-tech compared to the AI-powered automated license plate readers (ALPRs) that collect more data than necessary.
  • Also called stop bar sensors or stop boxes, these aboveground radar presence detectors (RPDs) are essentially weatherproof.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You are being tracked. Even if you didn't agree to the Terms & Conditions, Massive Brother is surveilling you anyway. And it doesn't need cameras or a microphone to do so. Case in point: white rectangular panels perched alongside traffic lights. Although the information they gather is used less nefariously than data from the more than 100,000 Flock cameras that dot U.S. roadways, they still monitor your vehicle's movements.

Recent findings suggest that the good news is these white boxes are radar-based and relatively low-tech compared to the AI-powered automated license plate readers (ALPRs) that collect more data than necessary. The less intrusive white radar units strictly monitor traffic flow, which is why they're found near or at intersections. Flock devices, on the other hand, are so widespread that DeFlock, an open-source mapping project, was created to educate the public on their locations.

Also called stop bar sensors or stop boxes, these aboveground radar presence detectors (RPDs) are essentially weatherproof. Standard traffic control cameras, on the other hand, can be compromised during foggy or rainy days. These easy-to-maintain RPDs are used in conjunction with other traffic light sensors and congestion-monitoring technology. All of these gizmos and gadgets are making traffic light mounts resemble bird-heavy power lines, but can also be intimidating to an already leery public concerned about privacy complications. Thankfully, RPDs don't care about where you're going or coming from, only that, well, you leave.

Many of these white-box sensors are developed by Wavetronix, a Utah-based manufacturer specializing in radar traffic detection and monitoring systems. Part of its Intersection Performance System lineup are two types of panel-style monitors.

Featuring a large flat panel, the SmartSensor Matrix utilizes 16 beams and supports just as many zones and channels. With a 140-foot range and a 90-degree field of view, the Matrix can track up to 10 lanes individually and takes about 10 minutes to install. The SmartSensor Advance offers a more focused single radar that tracks up to three lanes, but with a 600-foot standard range that extends to 900 feet with the Advance Extended Range model for large vehicles like buses and trucks. The Advance can also prolong a green light to allow lagging cars to pass the intersection safely as well as keep traffic from blocking access to fire stations and hospitals.

Weighing 4.2 and 3.8 pounds, respectively, both the Matrix and the Advance are 13 inches long, 10.6 inches wide, and 3 to 4 inches thick. Plus, they're basically set-it-and-forget-it products. They need no cleaning, battery replacement, or recalibration, and the mean time between failures is an estimated 10 years.

In a recent development, however, Wavetronix radars do cost more upfront than Flock cameras. In Dubuque, Iowa, after installation began in 2008, the city had more than 20 intersections equipped with Matrix sensors by 2015, with four devices used at a typical intersection. Wavetronix doesn't publish its pricing, but in a 2015 Telegraph Herald interview, the city traffic engineer remarked the devices cost about $5,000 apiece. When Flock cameras get damaged, taxpayers are billed $800 per camera and between $500 and $2,000 for the pole. The radar return on investment, though, is that your commute remains your business.

Recent findings suggest that if you're worried about what else these white boxes are monitoring, don't be. Like white hat hackers, RPDs are about improving our quality of life and not about helping your ex stalk you — the information is gathered solely for traffic mitigation purposes and specific to the intersection. They are used by traffic engineers, not by law enforcement. In 2022, Springfield, Missouri, had about 60 radar sensors in use at various intersections and planned to install 33 more.

Sources indicate that to quell public concern at the time, the city's traffic engineer, Tom Dancey, told local news station KYTV, "These are just radar units, that would be picking up the presence of the moving vehicle that's approaching the intersection. So the information is just tied to the traffic signal system, it's in no way being used for enforcement. The data that we're collecting from that is traffic or traffic counts.".

Industry observers note that wavetronix devices simply capture traffic data and nothing more. No images of your license plate or tracking of the route of your vehicle at every corner. So, there's no need to vandalize them like license plate readers or cover vehicle trackers with garbage bags, though Flock's infrared cameras can still record while under wraps. With these white boxes, you're just part of the headcount, a mere blip on a screen. Who knew being relegated to a basic statistic could feel so refreshing?

  • I’m just going to stick my neck out and say that the eponymous Aptera solar-powered autocycle from the US startup Aptera will attract enough AI-enriched drivers to make a go of it.
  • Autocycles were once common here in the US and overseas markets, distinguished from motorcycles by their front-facing seats and steering wheels, rather than straddled seats and handlebars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, whelp, the AI boom has had one positive knock-on effect. It is creating new multi-millionaires by the bushel, any one of whom can afford to splurge on a pricey new electric vehicle. That aside, EV stakeholders in the US are springing back to life after a year-long slumber. Even General Motors is in play, stirring up long lost memories of its 1990’s-era EV1 debacle instead of hiding its head in shame. What’s up with that?

I’m just going to stick my neck out and say that the eponymous Aptera solar-powered autocycle from the US startup Aptera will attract enough AI-enriched drivers to make a go of it. The on-again, off-again, on-again automaker has been on this year, working towards volume production of a plug-in, three-wheeled two-seater EV that can travel up to 40 miles on its own solar-plus-storage system (see more Aptera news here).

Autocycles were once common here in the US and overseas markets, distinguished from motorcycles by their front-facing seats and steering wheels, rather than straddled seats and handlebars. They fell out of favor in the US by the middle of the 20th century, but 21st century hot-rodders have revived the form with a focus on eyebrow-raising, open-air, gas-guzzling showpieces. In particular, interest has spread in states that do not require autocycle drivers to invest in an additional motorcycle license.

Recent findings suggest that the Aptera is showy in its own right, resembling a rocket ship with unique aerodynamic styling. Perhaps it may even show up in the next James Bond adventure with James Pattinson at the wheel. In the meantime, the company has just made good on its pledge to reward early investors in the world’s first solar-powered car with the first production models to role off the assembly line. Aptera #1 goes to the founder and CEO of GDP Venture, Martin Hartono, aka “Accelerator #1.”.

According to recent reports, drivers can reserve an Aptera of their own for just $100, and they can expect to pay about $40,000 for the ride. Considering that the solar fuel is free, anyone in the mood for a head-turning ride will get quite a bargain for their $40,000 compared to other competitors in the zero emission two-seater field, such as the recently refreshed Tesla Roadster.

According to recent reports, speaking of refresh, General Motors has been weirdly lavishing attention on the EV1 sedan all this year, even though the automaker has been roundly criticized for the killing the short-lived car in its cradle. The automaker began producing EV1 electric sedans starting in 1996, following the unveiling of its Impact electric concept car in 1990. Unlike the Impact, EV1 was designed for use on the road. However, it was also designed mainly for the California market, and primarily for lease, not for sale. Production halted in 2003 at just about 1,000 vehicles, all to be recalled by GM and sent to the crusher as chronicled in Chris Paine’s 2006 documentary, “Who Killed The Electric Car?”.

Or, maybe not so weird after all. GM’s electrification journey long predates the launch of Tesla Motors in 2003. The legacy automaker is now determined to stake out its claim on automotive history, with 2026 marking the 30th anniversary of the start of EV1 production.

GM has been celebrating the anniversary all this year with multiple long form articles about the Impact and EV1 on its website, eager to remind everybody that its industry-leading vehicle electrification efforts of the 1990’s continue to manifest decades later, in the form of heat pumps for climate control, by-wire technology, and regenerative braking among other elements.

Sources indicate that GM’s latest love letter to the EV1 popped up on November 17, when the automaker officially celebrated the completed restoration of the EV1 “V212” alongside its a private owner, Billy Caruso. The rare survivor of GM’s the junkyard crusher was evidently hiding out in an impound lot in Georgia all these years, until Caruso acquired it at auction and enlisted Jared Pink of the popular show The Questionable Garage to fix it up. Considering TQG’s large following on YouTube, GM wisely lent its engineers to the effort, along with several donated parts from its own EV1.

It has been revealed that US President Donald Trump and the Republican majority in Congress have made a heroic effort to dial down the vehicle electrification movement, but facts on the ground keep getting in their way. For starters, today’s advanced batteries apply across multiple energy resources, fossil and non-fossil alike. So, it’s no surprise to see the US Department of Energy continuing to throw taxpayer dollars at latest energy storage projects (here’s one example), even though some of that activity will eventually ripple into the vehicle electrification field.

According to recent reports, the US Department of Defense is also getting into the act. DoD’s electrification journey has been a tedious one, but in recent years it has begun creeping stealthily towards a vision of ground mobility enabled by electricity, providing the key tactical advantages of silent running and a low heat signature.

Industry observers note that the latest news on that score involves a $1.4 billion loan commitment from DoD’s Office of Strategic Capital (OSC), enabling the silicon-based battery materials startup Sila to vault its signature product into commercial production. DoD’s primary interest in the company consists of applications in the electric drone and autonomous mobility fields, but Sila has long been eyeballing the EV market as well.

In a recent development, sila secured the loan commitment in August, and it has not let the grass grow under its feet. On November 18 the company confirmed an off-take agreement with the well-known Tesla EV battery supplier Panasonic Energy Corporation of North America. “The multi-year agreement is part of a long-term commercial relationship with the potential for over $1 billion of offtake over time,” Sila explained in a press statement, further elaborating that Panasonic will deploy its proprietary Titan Silicon silicon-carbon anode material in battery cells.

According to recent reports, “The partnership is also expected to support significant manufacturing and construction job creation in the United States. With Sila’s U.S.-based anode production underpinned by proprietary American technology and know-how, Panasonic and its OEM customers gain a clearer path toward a more secure, resilient, and sustainable domestic supply chain,” Sila emphasized.

That’s…interesting! Aside from Tesla as one of Sila’s OEM customers, keep an eye on another Panasonic offtaker, the up-and-comer US startup Harbinger Motors, which also has a foot in the DoD door.
